also: if it is not out of place

terms.grammar: adjective; with ab and the ablative, or the dative; nōn aliēnum est (+ inf.), it is not out of place to
evidence: Nep. Milt. 6.1: nōn aliēnum vidētur, quāle praemium Miltiadī sit tribūtum, docēre (Lewis & Short)
Cic. de Or. 2.9: hoc aliēnum est (Lewis & Short s.v. aliquī)
Traupman 105: if it is not out of place, nisi aliēnum est
terms.comment: What belongs to someone else is out of place here: aliēnum est, it does not fit. An aside asking leave to say something: nisi aliēnum est, if it is not out of place.
Lewis & Short: in-aptus, “unsuitable, impertinent”; also silly.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 105, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
